entrypoints.summary: Kyber decapsulation accepting forged ciphertexts when an attacker can time its execution.
The public Cortex-M4 demonstration victim repeatedly receives a ciphertext and invokes crypto_kem_dec with a retained secret key; this is shared-mechanism evidence, not CIRCL integration evidence.

affected_components.role: Pre-fix integer division of coefficient-derived numerators and fixed-reciprocal replacement for compression widths 4, 5, 10, and 11.
Patch includes 105 added test lines; diff presence supports a regression-test addition, but the available inspected excerpt does not expose the individual assertions.

code_slices.fixed: For d=4/5 it multiplies the numerator by 315 and shifts right 20; for d=10/11 it multiplies by 20642679 and shifts right 36.
code_slices.surrounding_context: The patch documents Compress_q rounding semantics and bounds/rationale for the reciprocal approximations; it changes poly.go and adds test code in poly_test.go.
code_slices.vulnerable: For each affected width, CompressTo calculated uint16((((uint32(p[index]) << d) + uint32(Q)/2) / uint32(Q)) & mask).

negative_controls: Do not generalize the Cortex-M4 demo result to an unmodified CIRCL harness.
Ordinary ephemeral TLS usage is stated not to be affected.
observability.positive_marker: Timing differences correlate with selected ciphertext cases; the shared demo README reports 'Correctly guessed: 768' after processing its result file.

preconditions: A CIRCL Kyber keypair is reused.
The attacker can submit forged ciphertexts to a decapsulation operation.
The attacker can measure decapsulation timing.
The platform/compiler realizes the relevant division with timing dependent on the coefficient-derived numerator.

impact.attacker_capability: Submit forged ciphertexts to decapsulation, collect timing observations, and infer secret-dependent behavior; full-key recovery is demonstrated only for the shared KyberSlash2 mechanism on the paper/demo conditions.
impact.security_effect: Timing side channel permitting secret-key information disclosure under the disclosed forged-ciphertext timing-oracle and key-reuse preconditions.

causal_trace.summary: An attacker submits forged Kyber ciphertexts and observes decapsulation timing while the same keypair is reused.

Before the fix, Poly.CompressTo computed compression from normalized polynomial coefficients using a numerator derived from p coefficients and integer division by public Q for d values 4, 5, 10, and 11. The relevant numerator can be secret-derived during the decapsulation path, so its execution time must not depend on that value.
On some platform/compiler targets, the division is realized as variable-time division; crafted ciphertext choices produce timing differences that distinguish secret-dependent decapsulation behavior.

The maintainer disclosure states that timing forged-ciphertext decapsulation can reveal parts of the secret key. The reviewed KyberSlash2 method shows full secret-key recovery for the shared mechanism under its demonstrated conditions by choosing ciphertext parameters and comparing timing observations; that result is not a direct CIRCL end-to-end reproduction.

failure.operation: Integer division by Q in Poly.CompressTo for ciphertext-compression widths d=4,5,10,11.

primary_invariant.statement: Ciphertext-compression work reachable during decapsulation must not execute an operation whose latency varies with a secret-derived polynomial coefficient.
primary_invariant.violated_because: The pre-fix compression calculation divided ((coefficient << d) + Q/2) by Q. Although Q is public, the numerator incorporates a coefficient, and the commit identifies division by Q as timing-leaking on some platforms.

raw_refs.role: CIRCL remediation commit and code diff

quality.review_notes: CIRCL-specific scope is supported by the maintainer advisory and patch: affected through 1.3.6, fixed in 1.3.7, and timing exposure only on some platforms with forged-ciphertext decapsulation timing and key reuse. The paper and demo substantiate the shared KyberSlash2 mechanism and Cortex-M4 recovery workflow, but do not execute an unmodified CIRCL target. Ordinary ephemeral TLS use is explicitly excluded by the advisory/commit.

remediation.invariant_restored: Poly.CompressTo no longer uses division by Q for the affected compression widths; it uses fixed reciprocal multiplication and right shifts while retaining the documented compression result over the intended ranges.
mitigation_classes: replace secret-derived division with bounded reciprocal multiplication and shift
preserve compression output through arithmetic-range justification

oracle.channel: timing observations and recovered secret-coefficient guesses
oracle.expected_negative: A patched CIRCL build should retain compression output equivalence while removing the division operation from the affected CompressTo cases; no supplied artifact records a target-specific timing run proving this negative.
oracle.expected_positive: For the shared Cortex-M4 KyberSlash2 demonstration, crafted ciphertext timing observations support recovery of all 768 reported guesses from the supplied result data.
